mappings.note: Same definition: engineering the user-customised surface around a vendor harness, not building one.
Names the extension points (CLAUDE.md, skills, MCP, compression) that make up the integration surface.
RL on a specific tool set is where harness advantage lies; vendor-harness configurers do not get it.
Inner (model+tools) vs outer harness split; even a trivial outer loop pays.
Deterministic or non-deterministic code around a good harness; Ralph as proof.
One goal per context window as the fundamental behind recycling contexts.
Surfing the models: more context engineering on each new release; principles persist.
Evals are the durable asset; code around the model is cheap to throw away.
Failure is never looking at the returned data; do not automate what takes five seconds.
Tool formats trained on one harness degrade in another.
Exhaust the single-loop stack before adding an orchestration loop; Vaibhav's nested-loop speed counterpoint.
Keep trying dumb or futuristic things to keep capability understanding current (Simon Willison).
Adds the overfit failure of auto-research prompts (60 enumerated cases); needs production data and a human.
Dex says every team needs an AI code review bot; family says review bots mostly add noise.
Every engineer should hand-build an agent loop and read Claude Code/Codex source; no family covers this.
Design capabilities to be easy to delete as models improve; harness pieces expire.
Unopinionated harness plus production traces as eval set; fit harness to evals then human review.
Human inside the outer loop as intelligence injection; nuanced against on-the-loop framing.
Every feature has a metric and gradual rollout watched by a human; prod data prevents overfitting.
Control flow in prompts is a mistake; 2 hours of prompt vs 90-second script anecdote.
Headline takeaway: do not use prompts for control flow; keep an agentic escape hatch.

Capitalised emphasis does not buy compliance; split the prompt instead.

Editing a plan in-context applies feedback inconsistently; restart if one-shot plan is not ~95% right.
SDK splits design/structure/plan agents with schema outputs, forcing compaction at phase boundaries.
Inner Claude loop per phase with an outer deterministic harness checking structured output.

Dex's internal five/six-step split of RPI, but six slash commands to learn; UI should show next step.

Background verifier runs while human proceeds and interrupts only on a problem.
Two levers (fewer steps, more accurate selection); 99% over 20 steps compounding.
Ralph loop in the SDK with a structured-output exit decision instead of a bare bash loop.

PRD.json with todo/in-progress/done status enum so deterministic code orchestrates next story.
Zero build warnings to cut context bloat, plus dependency-boundary checks in CI.
Design docs as time-stamped checkpoints outside the repo; AI pass verifies review comments addressed.
Keep tight loops fast and push heavy verification to background tasks.
